question: Does every pair of models <=7B behave the same when they share a card - across load order, engine, family, concurrency and parallelism - or does the single ordered pair D7 measured generalise to nothing?
arms: co-residency, ollama beside ollama: ordered pairs of the 5 models <=7B held by BOTH rigs (qwen2.5-coder:1.5b 1.17G resident, qwen2.5-coder:3b ~2.3G, llama3.2:3b 2.55G, nemotron-3-nano:4b ~3.4G, qwen2.5-coder:7b ~5.7G). 5x4 = 20 ordered pairs per rig. ORDER IS AN ARM, not a nuisance: Finding 2c (serving-surface-2026-08-18/README.md:124) established placement is decided at load time and is STICKY, so (A then B) and (B then A) are different measurements.
cross-engine: the vLLM 1.5B AWQ beside each of the 5 ollama models, both orders - 10 per rig. This is the arm D7 never ran; its only co-residency cell was ollama beside ollama.

cross-family: carried by the pairs above rather than as a separate arm - the 5 models span 3 families (qwen2.5-coder, llama3.2, nemotron). Measured 2026-08-22 as possible on both rigs: llama3.2:3b and qwen2.5-coder:1.5b were both 100% on GPU together, 3722 MiB on srv1's 6144 and 3817 MiB on srv2's 12288.
concurrency and parallelability: a ramp per cell with the neighbour up, so the question is what a resident neighbour costs the width curve - not what the width curve is alone, which D7 already has.

cost.estimate_note: 30 cells per rig. srv1 at 13.7 min/cell and srv2 at 25.9 min/cell, from D7's survey phase (82 min / 6 cells and 285 min / 11 cells), multiplied by 1.5 because a co-residency cell carries two loads and a ramp where a survey cell carried one. Wall clock is the same number, not half: E14 refuses a second driver, so exactly one rig ever runs.
cost.comparison: D7 was 662 minutes. This is about 2.7x D7.

could_have_carried: the four D6 constants (START_TIMEOUT_S, DIGEST_TIMEOUT_S, LOAD_ATTEMPTS, RAMP_REPEATS) - every cell here is a load and a ramp, which is what measures all four
K7 (same model, both hosts, same geometry) and K9 (both hosts declare the residency settings) close on this campaign's evidence if it runs after 2026-08-22's rig changes
#329's cross-rig arm - the width-16 vLLM ramp per rig, ~19 min, if the vLLM cells here are launched through the same path
left_on_table: Unordered pairs instead of ordered would halve this to ~15 h, but load order IS the mechanism Finding 2c named, so dropping it measures the one thing already known and not the thing in question.

srv1 cannot hold 4 of the 10 unordered pairs (any pair with the 7B, and llama3.2:3b + nemotron-3-nano:4b at ~5.95G against 6144 MiB). Those cells are kept, not dropped: a refusal at load is cheap and is itself the placement datum.
Running both rigs at once is blocked by E14, not by the roster - launch.py refuses a second driver because one client timing two conversations degraded 12-21%.
Models >7B are out of scope by the question, so srv2's 8 larger models sit idle through all of it.
prerequisites: #322's gate, since this run must declare intent through it
the ollama settings declared on both rigs 2026-08-22: NUM_PARALLEL=0, MAX_LOADED_MODELS=0, KEEP_ALIVE=-1. MAX_LOADED_MODELS=0 is what permits any of this; srv1 previously capped at 3.
a vLLM gpu_memory_utilization low enough that an ollama model can land beside it - 0.85 has no recorded rationale and Finding 2c showed 0.90 pushed the neighbour to CPU
void_if: any cell's neighbour lands on CPU without the row saying so - Finding 2c's failure is silent, and size_vram 0.08 GB looked like a successful load
the two rigs' ollama versions still differ (srv1 0.32.4, srv2 0.32.5) and a cross-host difference is read as hardware - this is K6
load order is not recorded per cell
notes: Filed 2026-08-22 at the owner's instruction: 'test all possible combinations of models <=7B - co-residency, cross engine, cross family, concurrency, parallelability'. The inventory and every resident figure marked measured were read off the rigs that day; the ones marked ~ are scaled from disk size by the 1.17/0.986 and 2.55/2.0 ratios actually observed, and are estimates, not readings.
